skill.name: turnstile-spin
skill.description: Set up Cloudflare Turnstile across an existing frontend and backend. Create or recover widgets, protect selected requests, validate Siteverify, and support common frameworks.
skill.summary: Add and validate Cloudflare Turnstile protection in an existing application.
skill.author: cloudflare

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are safe Turnstile examples, bounded shell operations, or false matches on Markdown. Confirmed issues include plaintext home-directory token storage and mutable remote skill installation without integrity verification. The remote installation path can introduce unaudited instructions and executable scripts.

remediation.issue: Remote skill installation uses mutable content without integrity verification.
remediation.suggestion: Pin clones and downloads to an audited commit, verify a published SHA-256 digest, and install only the verified bundle.

remediation.issue: The workflow offers plaintext API token storage in a hidden home file.
remediation.suggestion: Use an operating-system credential store or platform secret manager. Remove the file option, or require explicit warning, expiry, and cleanup.

content.value_statement: Bot protection often fails when frontend widgets and server checks are configured separately. This skill coordinates creation, integration, secret handling, and validation.
actual_capabilities: Inspects an existing project for frontend frameworks, backend handlers, protected surfaces, and installed CAPTCHA providers.
Checks Cloudflare account access and verifies the token has Turnstile editing permission.
Creates a managed Turnstile widget for user-approved domains through the Cloudflare API.
Adds frontend widgets and server-side Siteverify checks for common web frameworks.
Validates widget metadata, secret ownership, action values, hostname allowlists, and token replay rejection.
Guides migration from standard reCAPTCHA or hCaptcha integrations while preserving existing handler behavior.
limitations: Requires an existing server-side handler because browser-only Siteverify is not secure.
Requires Cloudflare credentials with Turnstile editing permission and local command-line dependencies.
Does not add email delivery, databases, payments, OAuth, or unrelated infrastructure.
Cannot claim complete validation when the protected backend cannot run or receive a real token.

use_cases.title: Protect a signup flow
use_cases.description: Add a widget to signup and reject automated requests in the existing server handler.

use_cases.title: Migrate an existing CAPTCHA
use_cases.description: Replace reCAPTCHA or hCaptcha with Turnstile while preserving actions and backend behavior.

use_cases.title: Repair a partial integration
use_cases.description: Find missing hostname, action, secret, reset, or Siteverify checks and validate the corrected flow.

prompt_templates.title: Protect one form
prompt_templates.prompt: Add Cloudflare Turnstile to the signup form and its existing backend handler. Ask before creating resources or writing secrets.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs bot protection on one form.

prompt_templates.title: Protect selected actions
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan this project for user-triggered requests. Recommend which actions need Turnstile, then integrate only the actions I approve.
prompt_templates.scenario: A project contains several possible protection points.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate another CAPTCHA
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate the existing reCAPTCHA or hCaptcha integration to Turnstile. Preserve valid action names and existing business logic.
prompt_templates.scenario: An established application is changing CAPTCHA providers.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and repair Turnstile
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Turnstile integration end to end. Verify secret handling, expected actions, hostname allowlists, widget resets, and replay rejection before making approved fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs a security-focused integration review.

output_examples.input: Protect the signup form in this Next.js application from automated submissions.
output: Detected a Next.js App Router signup page and its server route.
Created one managed widget for the approved domains.
Added server validation for success, signup action, and approved hostnames.
Validation passed for the widget configuration and failed safely for a replayed token.

output_examples.input: Our contact form has a Turnstile widget, but submissions still bypass it.
output: The browser widget was present, but the server handler did not call Siteverify.
Added Siteverify before the existing contact logic and preserved the original handler.
Validation remains pending because the backend could not run locally.

best_practices: Use separate production hostname allowlists and exclude loopback addresses from production.
Keep the secret in an ignored environment file or managed secret store.
Validate success, action, hostname, and replay behavior before reporting completion.
anti_patterns: Do not call Siteverify from browser code or expose the secret to the client.
Do not run credential-bearing commands through project-local package executables.
Do not replace existing business logic when adding the verification gate.

faq.question: Does this skill create a Turnstile widget?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create a managed widget after account, domain, and user confirmation.

faq.question: Can it use an existing widget?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports guarded retrieval, validation, and storage for an existing widget.

faq.question: Which frameworks are documented?
faq.answer: The bundle includes examples for Next.js, Astro, SvelteKit, Hugo, and vanilla HTML backends.

faq.question: Does it work for a static site without a backend?
faq.answer: No. Secure Turnstile validation requires an existing server-side handler.

faq.question: Where is the Turnstile secret stored?
faq.answer: It uses an approved ignored environment file or the existing platform secret manager.

faq.question: What does validation cover?
faq.answer: It checks widget metadata, secret ownership, domains, actions, hostnames, successful requests, and token replay rejection.
